info.name: GraphX Connect API
info.description:
# GraphX Connect API

GraphX Connect (API-Hub) is the **agnostic integration hub** between wholesale suppliers (SanMar, S&S, 4Over, 994+ PromoStandards) and any consumer platform (GraphX Manage, OnPrintShop, Shopify, WooCommerce, n8n).

Connect **serves** everything it knows about suppliers — catalog, inventory, images, live cost, fulfillment status — and **accepts** orders to place with suppliers. It is platform-neutral: the same endpoints work for any consumer. **Manage is just the first consumer.**

## Getting Started
1. Set the collection variables: `base_url` (e.g. `http://localhost:8000` dev, or your prod host) and `orch_key` (your integration key).
2. Every request sends the header `X-Orchestrator-Key: {{orch_key}}`.
3. All bodies are JSON (`Content-Type: application/json`).

## Authentication
Machine callers authenticate with the **`X-Orchestrator-Key`** header, backed by the `integration_keys` table. (A Bearer-token layer is planned/optional — not the current mechanism.)

## Errors & Response Codes
Non-2xx responses use a uniform envelope: `{ "error": "<code>", "detail": "<reason>", "request_id": "req_..." }`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 401 | Missing / invalid `X-Orchestrator-Key` |
| 403 | Key lacks the required scope |
| 404 | Unknown supplier / product / order |
| 422 | Payload failed validation |
| 502 / 504 | Upstream supplier API error / timeout |

## Rate Limiting
Requests are rate-limited per integration key. On exceed, the API returns **429** with a `Retry-After` header.

## Pagination
List endpoints use `page` + `page_size` (default 50) and return `{ rows, total, page, page_size }`.

> **Status legend in this collection:** requests tagged **[LIVE]** exist today (use as-is). Requests tagged **[PLANNED]** are the agreed canonical contract to be built per the integration plan — they will 404 until implemented.

item.name: Authentication
item.description:
Connect's admin endpoints authenticate with the **`auth_token` session cookie** (set by login). Postman stores this cookie automatically after a successful Login and sends it on every later request.

> **Note for consumers / n8n:** a session cookie is fine for interactive use, but machine consumers need a stable key. The agnostic-API plan is to also accept `X-Orchestrator-Key` on these routes — see question bank Q4.

request.description: Authenticates a user and sets the `auth_token` cookie. Fill in your Connect email + password, then Send. After 200, every other request in this collection is authenticated automatically (Postman re-sends the cookie). Returns the current user.

item.name: Catalog
